clarity.justification: The central test is logically aligned with the hypothesis: the plan will "extract residual-stream hidden states" and measure when a probe prediction "matches final answer and remains stable," followed by accuracy-versus-token comparisons against explicit baselines. The directional expectation of "25-45% token reduction at near-equal accuracy" supplies a quantified efficiency target, and failure to achieve that reduction without an accuracy loss would refute the early-exit claim, although "near-equal" is not numerically defined. Important gaps remain: the retrospective commitment definition uses knowledge of the eventual answer, the transition from "per-step linear probes" to an online "single lightweight probe" is underspecified, and "rare = post-hoc" does not by itself establish post-hoc rationalization.

feasibility.justification: The named models and datasets—"Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, and Llama-3.1-8B" with "GSM8K, MATH, ProntoQA, ARC"—exist, and residual-stream extraction, linear probing, logit-lens readouts, and token-level generation control are supported by standard tooling. The hardest step is converting an online probe prediction into an emitted open-ended answer: "bucketed/token-matched answer" and then "force '\nThe answer is' continuation" does not specify how arbitrary or multi-token numeric answers are decoded, so this is custom logic bordering on an undefined step, whereas the MCQ version is standard. The design includes runnable negative-result controls through full-CoT, fixed-truncation, entropy, and self-consistency baselines plus layer/window/transfer ablations, but resources are only partly quantified—model sizes and an expected "25-45%" saving are given, while sample counts, selected layers, K, W, and calibration-set sizes are absent.
